findings.description: The bucket is explicitly commented as public with no ACL, bucket policy, or public access block to restrict access, exposing all objects to the internet.

No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so customer data is stored unencrypted on the S3 service-side default (which may be AES256 but not KMS-managed), and the file itself is cleartext as uploaded.
The object containing customer-master.xlsx (likely sensitive customer data) is uploaded with no server-side encryption applied, leaving it stored unencrypted.
The object is placed in the public 'data' bucket with no object ACL or policy restricting access, so the customer spreadsheet is readable by anyone.
The financials bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, storing financial data in cleartext at rest.
The operations bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, storing operational data unencrypted at rest.
The data_science bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, storing data unencrypted at rest.
